preamble: Raising and rounding of the open vowel [a] (here the open back [ɑ]/[ɒ]) to the close back rounded [u]. In colloquial Iranian Persian, especially the Tehrani standard, historical ā (modern [ɒː]) is raised to [u] before the nasals /n/ and, in a smaller set of words, /m/, so that nān 'bread' becomes nun and hammām 'bath' becomes hamum. Persian studies trace the process back to Middle Persian.

examples.note: Historical ā ([ɒː]) is raised to [u] before /n/ in most words in colloquial speech. The from forms are the standard literary pronunciation, which keeps the conservative ā [ɒː].
Before /m/ the raising affects a limited set of words, such as tamām > tamum 'finished' and bādām > bādum 'almond'.

sources: University of Texas at Austin (2007). Persian Online: What is Diglossia? https://sites.la.utexas.edu/persian_online_resources/language-specific-grammar/diglossia/
